elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads "Customer may solicit, hire, or employ Vendor employees without restriction." — the one-sided bar on soliciting/hiring/employing Vendor employees for the term plus 24 months is gone, and no other cited provision imposes a solicitation restraint on Customer (§ 12.3 affirmatively confirms no no-hire commitment).
No covenant survives in either direction; § 12.4 as rendered imposes nothing on Vendor, so there is no mutual restriction. Not a defect on the chosen preferred path.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: No restriction exists to be scoped to Services personnel; the rendered text is a pure permission for Customer.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: No duration language remains (deterministic check: "number not found"), because there is no surviving covenant to date-limit. Moot on the preferred path.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no restriction on Customer, general advertisements are unrestricted a fortiori, and § 12.3 preserves "hiring any person who responds to general recruitment." The failed deterministic carve-out check has no subject.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no covenant restrains Customer's response to unsolicited approaches; the offending "regardless of how the employee applies" language has been deleted.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The no-hire wording ("hire, or employ") is removed as a prohibition and now appears only as an express permission for Customer.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is satisfied by the rewritten § 12.4, which eliminates the solicitation, hiring and employment restraint on Customer.
Fallback level is incomplete (no mutual, involvement-limited, 12-month covenant exists), but that is irrelevant because the redline targets and fully achieves the preferred position.

The two failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are inapplicable on the preferred path — no surviving covenant needs a term limit or a carve-out — so they do not defeat position-completeness.
Minimal: only § 12.4's operative words changed; no survival tail, procedure, damages category, or unrelated obligation was added, and the favourable § 12.3 acknowledgement is retained untouched.

Preserves intent: the edit removes an internal conflict with § 12.3 rather than creating one, leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and the separate non-compete provision is left to its own rule.

Drafting nit only (not a completeness defect): a simple deletion of § 12.4 would achieve the same result; the affirmative "may ... without restriction" formulation is slightly broader in expression but imposes no obligation on Customer and duplicates no operative term.
